findings.passage: “I think that in our Legislature the past few years we’ve done a good job of crafting and passing laws that have helped maintain the integrity of elections in Mississippi,” Senator Tate said. “When there’s questions that come about in elections, I think Mississippi is the last place where there’s question marks.”
findings.note: Quoted by Magnolia Tribune (article date; spoken that week) while announcing a run for Secretary of State. General statement about state election-integrity laws; names no ID or citizenship rule.

findings.passage: “Being a former election commissioner for 10 years and past chairman of the Senate Elections Committee, I have a passion and understanding of how we can move Mississippi forward regarding elections,” Tate said.
findings.note: Quoted by Magnolia Tribune on his background for the Secretary of State race. No specific ID or citizenship rule named.

findings.passage: “The rationale is to clean our voter rolls, make sure that we maintain good voter rolls.  A lot of  legislations out there dictates how much counties have to spend on elections based on their active voter roll.  With inflating books were going to have more costs that go down to the counties,” said Tate.
findings.note: Quoted by Mississippi Public Broadcasting during Senate debate on SB 2588 (2021), his bill to start removal of voters who miss two years of voting after a postcard goes unanswered.

findings.passage: “It’s there I promise you,” said Tate.
findings.note: Quoted by MPB answering a colleague who asked whether there was evidence of voter fraud, in the debate on SB 2588; he added he did not have the evidence with him.
